implementation_statement: The owner holds one named administrator account in each service. Subscriber admins create and remove their own staff accounts in the product. Gap: the support contractor signs in to the admin console with the owner's super-admin login, so there is no separate account to disable or review, and SaaS accounts are never reviewed.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(n); FTC Start with Security 2)

implementation_statement: Tenant isolation is enforced in application code: every database query is scoped by account ID through one shared query helper. Gap: no automated test proves that one subscriber cannot reach another subscriber's records, and uploaded photos are served through public links that never expire.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (FTC Start with Security 5); Customer DPA (use only to provide the service)

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the owner-developer holds every role, including system administrator. The outside accountant (CPA firm) reviews the bookkeeping with access to the accounting SaaS only, and subscription billing runs through the payment processor's hosted checkout. Gap: the support contractor signs in to the admin console with the owner's super-admin login until a named support role with view-only access is built (due 2026-11-30, POAM-003).
Only the owner should hold super-admin rights. The contractor will get a named support role in the admin console that can view but not export subscriber data, with its own MFA, by 2026-11-30.

The product limits failed sign-ins to 10 per account per 15 minutes and slows repeated attempts from one address (framework rate limiting). The hosting provider and SaaS vendors apply their own limits to administrator sign-ins.

The owner is self-taught and has had no security training. The owner completes an annual security awareness course and a secure coding course by 2026-12-31; the support contractor completes a short awareness module before the new support role is issued.

The hosting provider logs console and API events for 30 days; the application logs sign-ins, failed sign-ins, and errors. Gap: admin console actions (opening, editing, or exporting a subscriber account) are not logged at all.
evidence: Hosting audit log screen; application log sample

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Nobody reviews the hosting audit log, the repository security log, or failed sign-ins. Starting 2026-10, the owner reviews them on the first business day of each month with a one-page checklist and exports the hosting log so 12 months are kept.

Compensating control (one-person business): the owner is the only administrator, so the logs stay with the providers. The hosting provider keeps its account audit log of console and API events for 30 days on its own platform, outside the laptop. Gap: admin console actions are not logged at all, and the hosting log is kept only 30 days until the monthly export starts (POAM-007).

Compensating control (one-person business): the P07 plan states openly that independence is limited, because the owner designed, operates, and assessed the controls. POL-01 4.5 requires every yearly evaluation to include at least one day of challenge and testing by an outside consultant who does not operate the controls. The contract security consultant did this on 2026-08-27, with no stake in the result and no standing access. The hosting provider's SOC 2 Type 2 report, reviewed 2026-09-09, covers its inherited controls.
evidence: P07 assessment plan; POL-01 4.5; consultant notes 2026-08-27; P09 vendor review

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): no second reviewer is possible, so under CM-3(g) the repository and CI pipeline are the change control element. POL-01 9.1 requires every change to go through the repository and CI, with nothing deployed by hand except in an incident under P08. About 1,100 automated tests run on every push. P09 CC8.1 names the planned compensating steps: tenant isolation and authorization tests (due 2027-03-31) and outside review of high-risk changes when the standby developer is engaged. Gap: no security or isolation tests yet.

Platform defaults are secure (HTTPS only, managed certificates, encrypted storage). The consultant's review on 2026-08-27 found photo objects served through public links with no expiry and the database accepting connections from any address with a password. Signed, expiring links and a database allow list by 2026-11-30.
The BIA (P05), POL-01 section 11, and the P08 runbook form the contingency plan. Gap: the sealed emergency access kit and the standby developer arrangement are not in place (due 2026-12-31).

First restore test on 2026-08-27: point-in-time restore of the database to a scratch instance in 2 hours 10 minutes, witnessed by the consultant. Gap: no test frequency was set before the test and photo storage restore was not tested. POL-01 11.3 now sets an annual test each August.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01; website statement "automatic backups every day"

implementation_statement: The provider takes daily database backups kept 7 days and offers 7-day point-in-time recovery (inherited). Owner responsibility: backups sit in the same provider account that the CI token can administer, photo uploads have no versioning or backup, and no copy exists outside the account.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01; website statement "automatic backups every day"

implementation_statement: The owner has a named account in every service, and each subscriber staff member has a unique product account. Gap: the contractor signs in to the admin console as the owner.

implementation_statement: Authenticator-app MFA is on for the hosting console, source repository, business email, password manager, and payment processor. Gap: the domain registrar account and the product's own admin console use a password only. Owner turns on registrar MFA by 2026-10-15 and adds MFA to the admin console by 2026-11-30.
evidence: Account security pages; P07 sign-in tests 2026-08-27

implementation_statement: Owner passwords are unique and stored in the password manager. Subscriber passwords are salted and hashed by the framework with an 8-character minimum. Gap: production secrets (hosting token, database password, API keys) have never been rotated; the CI token is long-lived; subscriber passwords are not checked against known breached passwords.

Production secrets are stored in the hosting platform's encrypted settings and as CI secrets, but also in a plaintext .env file on the laptop. An old, revoked token was found in the public demo repository's history. The owner moves local secrets into the password manager's secrets feature, deletes the .env file, turns on repository secret scanning with push protection, and rotates every secret by 2026-10-31. Added because P01 R-001 and the P08 scenario turn on this weakness.

The DPA sets when subscribers are told (72 hours; 48 hours for two), and the P08 notification matrix lists every external notice. Gap: the support contractor has no duty or time limit to report suspected incidents, and there is no subscriber security contact list (due 2026-10-31).
regulatory_driver: Customer DPA; Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)(a); N51-R01 (FTC Data Breach Response)

implementation_statement: The P08 runbook and notification matrix were adopted on 2026-09-25. Gap: not yet walked through; breach counsel not identified; no list of subscriber security contacts with the two 48-hour customers flagged (due 2026-10-31).
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (FTC Data Breach Response); Customer DPA (72-hour and 48-hour notice); Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)

implementation_statement: First risk assessment completed 2026-08-28 using NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). Reviewed each August and after major changes (POL-01 4.3).

Repository dependency alerts are on. Gap: 14 alerts were open on 2026-08-27 (2 high severity), nobody triages them, and the running application has never been scanned. Monthly triage with fix times (high 14 days, others 30 days) and a quarterly web application scan.

Sub-processors are used on their standard online terms; the hosting provider and email service terms include a DPA. Gap: no DPA with the AI model provider, which is also missing from the public sub-processor list; no provider SOC 2 report was reviewed before 2026-09-09; the contractor agreement has no security terms.
evidence: Vendor terms folder; P09 vendor review
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (FTC Start with Security 8); Customer DPA (sub-processor notice)

implementation_statement: Unit and integration tests run in CI on every push (about 1,100 tests). Gap: no tests for tenant isolation, authorization, or the export and deletion features, and no security testing of the running application.

The platform exposes only HTTPS on its public endpoints; the provider runs the edge routing and network isolation (inherited). The owner keeps the job worker private and exposes no other ports. Database network exposure is tracked under CM-6.

TLS 1.2 or higher protects all web and API traffic with managed certificates (inherited). Gap: subscriber data exports are emailed as CSV attachments. Replace with expiring download links from the admin console by 2026-11-30.

The provider encrypts the database, backups, and object storage at rest (inherited). Laptop full-disk encryption is on; the phone is encrypted by its passcode. The plaintext .env file and the local database copy are protected only by disk encryption; those weaknesses are tracked under IA-5(7) and P03 G-003.
evidence: Hosting encryption settings; laptop encryption status (P07)
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (FTC Start with Security 4); website statement "bank-level 256-bit encryption"

implementation_statement: The provider patches the platform runtime and the managed database. The owner updates the framework about monthly. Gap: no defined fix times, and 2 high-severity dependency alerts were open on 2026-08-27.
